notes: Nim compiles to C and needs a C compiler at build time on every OS; none of the Linux/macOS archives bundle one and the Windows zips do not either (MinGW is a separate nim-lang.org download that finish.exe fetches). Zig: Nim has no built-in zig entry (checked extccomp.nim in 0.20.2, 1.6.20, 2.2.12). `zig cc` can stand in through a one-line wrapper (zigcc = `zig cc "$@"`, zigcc.cmd = `@zig cc %*`) with --cc:clang --clang.exe:zigcc --clang.linkerexe:zigcc; tested on Linux amd64 with Zig 0.13.0 for 0.20.2, 1.6.20 and 2.2.12 (hello world built and ran, wrapper in a path with a space), and 2.2.12 also cross-compiled a Windows x86_64 exe with --os:windows --cpu:amd64 and -target x86_64-windows-gnu in --passC/--passL. Set ZIG_GLOBAL_CACHE_DIR/ZIG_LOCAL_CACHE_DIR, or Zig caches in ~/.cache/zig. Zig is itself a ~47 MB self-contained archive that could live in {runtime_dir}, so it is a way to make Linux fully self-contained and to avoid installing Xcode CLT on macOS (zig ships macOS libc stubs; untested on a Mac). It does not help Windows XP: current Zig needs Windows 10. Package manager: nimble ships in every archive; keep packages in {runtime_dir}\nimble via --nimbleDir. All tests were run as an unprivileged user on Linux amd64 only.

prerequisites: glibc 2.3+ for bin/nim, 2.7+ for bin/nimble (dynamically linked)
git on PATH, only for nimble installs of remote packages
recipes.notes: Tested as a normal user: unpacked twice side by side under paths with spaces ('app one/rt/0.20.2', 'app two/rt/0.20.2'), compiled and ran hello world with system gcc 13.3 from both; nimble 0.10.2 installed a local package (with a `requires "nim >= 0.19.0"` line) into "{runtime_dir}/nimble pkgs" via --nimbleDir and the compiler found it via --nimblePath. Nothing was written to HOME. The archive also carries build.sh/c_code (not needed). Nim finds lib/ and config/ relative to bin/nim, so moving the folder works. Isolation at run time: pass --skipUserCfg (otherwise ~/.config/nim/nim.cfg and config.nims are read into the private compiler; tested, a define placed there was picked up) and --nimcache:<app dir> (default is $XDG_CACHE_HOME/nim or ~/.cache/nim/<project>_d). Find packages with NIMBLE_DIR={runtime_dir}/nimble in the compiler's environment (the compiler then replaces every nimblepath from nim.cfg with $NIMBLE_DIR/pkgs2 and /pkgs, so ~/.nimble is not searched) or with --nimblePath:"{runtime_dir}/nimble/pkgs2" --nimblePath:"{runtime_dir}/nimble/pkgs". Always use nimble --nimbleDir:<dir> rather than the NIMBLE_DIR variable for nimble itself: with NIMBLE_DIR nimble 0.24 (Nim 2.2) still puts its download cache in ~/.nimble/pkgcache, and with neither it writes ~/.nimble even for `nimble --version`. nimble reads ~/.config/nimble/nimble.ini (%APPDATA%\nimble\nimble.ini on Windows) if present; run it with HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME pointing at {tmp} during install to be safe. nimble needs git on PATH for remote packages (not bundled). Compiled programs are ordinary native executables; they need the C compiler only at build time. Added 2026-09-20 (design.md 11.0 item 15): on Linux the C toolchain is zig, a companion runtime (policy `requires`), not the system compiler, so an unattended install needs no root and works on a machine with no gcc at all. The steps write a small POSIX shim into {runtime_dir}/ibcc under every name a build might call (cc, gcc, clang, c++, g++, clang++, ar); it execs `zig cc`/`zig c++`/`zig ar` and rewrites a Rust target triple (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu) to zig's (x86_64-linux-gnu), which cc-rs passes as --target= and zig's parser rejects. {runtime_dir}/ibcc goes first on PATH for the project install only. Tested on this machine with only the shim on PATH: cargo built a crate with a cc-rs build step and ran it, and nim compiled and linked a program using std/httpclient.

steps.text: # zig as this app's C toolchain, so an unattended install needs no root
# and no system compiler (design.md 11.0 item 15). The name it is called
# by picks the mode, and a Rust target triple is rewritten to zig's
case ${0##*/} in *++) m=c++ ;; ar) m=ar ;; *) m=cc ;; esac

steps.run: cd "{runtime_dir}/ibcc" && chmod 755 cc && for t in gcc clang c++ g++ clang++ ar; do cp cc "$t"; done

prerequisites: Xcode Command Line Tools (clang, SDK headers). Nim invokes `clang` on macOS (build.sh and nim.cfg use clang). Installing CLT is system-wide and outside {runtime_dir} (`xcode-select --install` opens a GUI prompt; unattended installs use softwareupdate with the CLT label), so treat it as a machine prerequisite, not part of the runtime.
recipes.notes: No macOS binary exists for 0.20, so it is built in place from the source tarball (the same tarball used for any Unix). build.sh compiles the pre-generated C in c_code/ into bin/nim with clang (set CC to override); `koch boot` is optional (it rebuilds the compiler from Nim, already done by build.sh for a release tarball) and `koch tools` builds nimble (from the bundled dist/nimble, no network), nimsuggest, nimgrep and nimpretty. Tested on Linux as a proxy (amd64, gcc 13.3, path with a space): the same three commands succeeded in about 7 minutes (most of it `koch tools`) and the result compiled hello world; not run on a Mac. Apple Silicon caveat (read from build.sh, untested): `uname -m` is `arm64`, which matches build.sh's `*arm*` case before `*aarch64*`, so plain `sh build.sh` picks 32-bit ARM C sources and fails; `--cpu aarch64` selects the arm64 sources, but 0.20.2 has no official Apple Silicon support, so the safer choice on an M-series Mac is an x86_64 build under Rosetta 2 (`arch -x86_64 sh build.sh`, then everything including compiled apps is x86_64). koch writes a nimcache for itself; the HOME/XDG_* exports keep that and nimble's first-run files out of root's home. Isolation at run time: pass --skipUserCfg (otherwise ~/.config/nim/nim.cfg and config.nims are read into the private compiler; tested, a define placed there was picked up) and --nimcache:<app dir> (default is ~/.cache/nim (XDG_CACHE_HOME if set)/<project>_d). prerequisites: MinGW-w64 GCC, a SEPARATE download not in the zip: https://nim-lang.org/download/mingw64.7z (62,290,033 bytes, sha256 04a535d1e0880364ca9609713744f1a9a36835c4ced834cf435c4dc4eca2159a) or https://nim-lang.org/download/mingw32.7z (61,793,563 bytes, sha256 588794e11be36389501610cf78de777e52a920e03db256ee8bd1a7c2c45e39a4). Both are WinLibs GCC 11.1.0 / MinGW-w64 8.0.2 builds (2021-05). The 7z uses the BCJ2 filter, so the base installer's 7z decoder must support BCJ2.
git on PATH, only for nimble remote packages (not bundled)
recipes.notes:
The zip does NOT include a C compiler: only nim.exe, nimble.exe, the other tools and runtime DLLs (OpenSSL 1.1, PCRE, SQLite, SDL2, etc.) in bin\. finish.exe is an interactive post-install helper that adds bin\ to the user PATH in the registry, creates Start-menu shortcuts and offers to download mingw<bits>.7z into dist\ and unpack it with bin\7zG.exe, then patches config
im.cfg with an ABSOLUTE gcc.path. Do not run it (PATH, shortcuts, absolute path). Instead: unpack the zip, unpack the MinGW 7z into {runtime_dir}\dist (it contains a single top folder, mingw64\ or mingw32\), and point Nim at it with a relative setting in the system config.nims, which Nim reads from {runtime_dir}\config next to nim.cfg. thisDir() is the folder of that config.nims, so the setting survives moving the folder and works with spaces. Tested on Linux with a wrapper compiler in dist/mingw64/bin for 0.20.2, 1.6.20 and 2.2.12 (0.20.2 has no config.nims, and the append creates it, which also worked); not run on Windows. For the x86 zip, replace mingw64 with mingw32 in the cmd step. In that cmd line the & must stay escaped as ^& (it sits outside quotes); a % in {runtime_dir} would be expanded by cmd, so the installer should reject or escape it. Nim does not expand $nim in gcc.path, and the commented `#gcc.path = r"$nim\dist\mingw in"` line in nim.cfg is only a search string for finish.exe. Adding {runtime_dir}\dist\mingw64 in to the PATH of the app's own process works too. MinGW is self-contained: cc1.exe has its DLLs beside it in libexec, so it does not need to be on PATH. Programs built with -d:ssl, the re module (PCRE), db_sqlite and similar load DLLs from bin\ at run time; ship the ones the app needs next to the app's exe, because {runtime_dir} in is not on PATH. Run-time isolation on Windows: nimcache defaults to %USERPROFILE%
imcache\<project>_d (pass --nimcache), user config is %APPDATA%
im
im.cfg and config.nims (pass --skipUserCfg), nimble defaults to %USERPROFILE%\.nimble (pass --nimbleDir; compile with NIMBLE_DIR set or --nimblePath) and reads %APPDATA%
imble
imble.ini. 0.20.2's finish.exe still points at mingw<bits>-6.3.0.7z, which now returns 404 on nim-lang.org, so the current GCC 11.1 archive is the only official one; generated C from 0.20 compiling cleanly with GCC 11 is untested. nimble 0.10.2 handled paths with spaces in Linux tests.
recipes.min_os: Compiler (bin\nim.exe) runs on Windows XP (PE subsystem 4.0 on x86, 5.2 on x64; imports only KERNEL32 and msvcrt with no post-XP functions, and inet_ntop is emulated below Vista). The bundled-by-download MinGW (GCC 11.1) needs Vista+: its libzstd-1.dll, loaded by cc1.exe, imports InitializeConditionVariable. nimble.exe 0.10.2 has no post-XP imports. So a working compile needs Vista or later unless an XP-capable MinGW is supplied.

Both are WinLibs GCC 11.1.0 / MinGW-w64 8.0.2 builds (2021-05). The 7z uses the BCJ2 filter, so the base installer's 7z decoder must support BCJ2.
git on PATH, only for nimble remote packages (not bundled)
recipes.notes: Nim for Windows as its own installer (finish.exe) sets it up: the zip plus Nim's dlls.zip (OpenSSL 1.1, PCRE, SQLite, pdcurses DLLs; policy extra_files) in bin, unpacked with Windows's tar.exe (10 1803+) or the shell's zip folder support (7, 8.1), and a current cacert.pem there too (dlls.zip's is from 2021). Without the DLLs a program built with -d:ssl stops at start: could not load: (libcrypto-1_1-x64|libeay64).dll (tested 2026-09-19).

steps.run: ("%SystemRoot%\System32\tar.exe" -xf "{tmp}\dlls.zip" -C "{runtime_dir}\bin" 2>nul || powershell -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command "$s = New-Object -ComObject Shell.Application; $s.NameSpace('{runtime_dir}\bin').CopyHere($s.NameSpace('{tmp}\dlls.zip').Items(), 20)") || (echo Nim's DLLs ^(OpenSSL, PCRE, SQLite^) could not be unpacked: programs using -d:ssl won't start. & ver >nul)

recipes.min_os: Compiler (bin\nim.exe) runs on Windows XP (PE subsystem 4.0 on x86, 5.2 on x64; imports only KERNEL32 and msvcrt with no post-XP functions, and inet_ntop is emulated below Vista). The bundled-by-download MinGW (GCC 11.1) needs Vista+: its libzstd-1.dll, loaded by cc1.exe, imports InitializeConditionVariable. nimble.exe 0.24.1 needs Vista+ (it loads CreateSymbolicLinkW and GetQueuedCompletionStatusEx from kernel32 at startup through Nim's dynlib mechanism, which quits if a symbol is missing). So a working compile needs Vista or later unless an XP-capable MinGW is supplied.
sources: tools/finish.nim and config/nim.cfg inside the zips (read locally)

launch.notes: The app is the program built by project_install and runs directly, with the runtime's bin folder on PATH: Nim programs load OpenSSL (-d:ssl), PCRE (std/re) and SQLite (db_sqlite) as DLLs at run time, and std/net looks for cacert.pem on PATH.
